title: Markdown fence with prose around it
input:
Here is the JSON you requested:

```json
{"name": "Ada", "score": 42}
```

Let me know if you need anything else.
notes: Chat-style answer: prose before and after a ```json fence. Only the fenced value is data. Failure class: structured_output (sibling atlas: https://github.com/Qin-Z-x/llm-failbench/blob/main/data/evidence/structured_output.jsonl).

title: Single-quoted strings
notes: Python-repr style output. Single-quoted strings are not JSON and must be converted.

title: Curly (smart) quotes around keys and values
notes: Word-processor or chat UI turned ASCII quotes into curly quotes.

title: Unquoted (bare) object keys
notes: JavaScript object-literal style; bare identifier keys need quoting.

title: Trailing comma inside an object
notes: A single trailing comma before the closing brace.

title: Trailing comma inside an array
notes: Trailing comma in a nested array.

title: Line (//) comments inside the object
notes: JSONC-style line comments, including a comment after a value.

title: Block (/* */) comments inside the object
notes: JSONC-style block comment between members.

title: Python True/False/None literals
notes: Python literal spellings instead of JSON true/false/null.

title: NaN and Infinity values
notes: Non-finite floats are not valid JSON; repaired lossily to null with a warning. The bare keys also exercise key quoting so the document takes the repair path.

title: Truncated nested object (two open depths)
notes: Output cut off at the end of a nested object: close both containers. Failure class: structured_output (sibling atlas: https://github.com/Qin-Z-x/llm-failbench/blob/main/data/evidence/structured_output.jsonl).

title: Truncated array of objects
notes: Output cut off inside an object nested in an array; close object then array.

title: Truncated object with incomplete trailing token
notes: Only the incomplete trailing member is dropped; complete members are kept.

title: Duplicate object keys
notes: Last duplicate value wins deterministically, with a warning.

title: Multiple candidate objects in prose
input: The safest payload is {"name": "Ada", "score": 42}. Do not use {"name": "Ada", "score": 41} for the final answer.
notes: Two complete objects appear in prose; extraction is deterministic (first complete value) and records an ambiguity warning.

title: UTF-8 BOM before the document
notes: A byte-order mark glued to the front of the document by a text pipeline.

title: Escaped newline and tab sequences in strings
notes: Valid JSON \n and \t escapes must survive fence stripping and decode to real newline/tab characters.

title: Unicode values (Chinese, Arabic, emoji)
notes: Non-ASCII values must round-trip exactly (no mojibake, no unnecessary escaping).

title: Top-level JSON array (scalar elements)
notes: A top-level scalar array (not an object) with a trailing comma before the closing bracket.

title: Deep nesting: 20 levels
notes: Twenty nested arrays with a trailing comma at the innermost level; depth must not be silently truncated.

title: Schema-guided numeric-string coercion
notes: Schema-directed coercion: quoted integers/numbers become JSON numbers only because the schema says so.

title: Schema-guided boolean-string coercion
notes: Quoted booleans are coerced only when the schema declares boolean.

title: Unknown properties removed (additionalProperties=false)
notes: A key not declared by the schema is dropped because additionalProperties is false; a warning is recorded.

title: Missing required property (expected failure)
notes: Schema requires email, which is absent; repair must not invent field values, so ok=false. Failure class: structured_output (sibling atlas: https://github.com/Qin-Z-x/llm-failbench/blob/main/data/evidence/structured_output.jsonl).

title: Enum violation (expected failure)
notes: status is outside the declared enum; a parsed document that fails validation is returned as ok=false, not coerced.

title: Numeric minimum violation (expected failure)
notes: quantity is below schema minimum 5; validation failure is reported rather than clamping the value.

title: Empty input (expected failure)
notes: No JSON value at all; ok=false with an 'unparseable:' warning.

title: Whitespace-only input (expected failure)
notes: Only whitespace is present; there is no JSON value to repair.

title: Plain prose without JSON (expected failure)
input: Sure! I'd be happy to help. Tell me which fields you need and I will format them for you.
notes: Conversational refusal/offer with no JSON value; must fail rather than fabricate an object.

title: Stray control characters around the document
notes: Stray NUL/BEL control bytes surrounding an otherwise valid document are removed before parsing.

title: JavaScript undefined value
notes: JavaScript undefined is not JSON; repaired to null (never invented).

title: Leading plus sign on numbers
notes: JavaScript-style numeric literals with a leading + sign.

title: Invalid \x hex escapes in strings
notes: JavaScript \xHH escapes are not JSON; sanitized to the equivalent characters.

title: Single trailing comma after the root value at EOF
notes: A stray comma follows the root object at end of input; the root value is recovered after removing the trailing comma.

title: Misquoted keys containing spaces
notes: Keys containing spaces are single-quoted (wrong quote type); they must be converted as whole keys.

title: Colons inside quoted strings
notes: A key/value splitter must not split on colons that occur inside quoted strings.

title: URL containing // next to a line comment
notes: // inside a JSON string is not a comment; only the real trailing comment is removed.

title: Nested markdown fences (inner fence inside a string)
notes: The outer fence wraps a JSON string that itself contains ``` markers; the stripper must match the outer fence and keep escaped newlines.

title: JSON value embedded in XML/HTML markup
notes: Structured answer wrapped in XML-ish tags; the embedded JSON value is extracted.

title: Two JSON objects concatenated
notes: Two complete top-level values with no separator; deterministic policy is first value wins with warning multiple_json_values:first_used.

title: JSON Lines (JSONL) document
notes: One JSON object per line is a JSONL stream; deterministic policy is first value wins (never ok=false) with warning multiple_json_values:first_used.

title: Extremely long numeric array (200 elements)
notes: Two hundred numeric elements with a trailing comma; long arrays must not be truncated or misparsed.

title: Large (~100 KB) document with one trailing comma
notes: Roughly 100 KB of indented nested data with a single trailing comma after the root object at EOF; the root value is recovered whole.
